text:
Adrian Kempe scored three times, and Kenny Connors, a third-round pick out of Dubuque who played at UMass last season, picked up his first NHL point on Erik Haula's goal as the Kings beat the Sharks 7-2 at Crypto.com Arena. The Sharks had won the first meeting this season in overtime, 5-4 on Oct. 3, and this one went the other way early. Kempe scored 83 seconds in, added a slap shot late in the first, and completed the hat trick on a power play in the second.

Our numbers say LAK deserved most of it. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count, favored LAK 3.94 to 2.56, and by our simulation of every shot, LAK wins that game 71 percent of the time. The Kings built it in the first period, out-chancing SJS 2.08 to 1.05 and leading 3-0 after Quinton Byfield scored on the power play with 82 seconds left. Artemi Panarin, who joined the Kings as an undrafted free agent, set up four goals. SJS actually had more shot attempts, 67 to 57, but LAK blocked 19 shots to 12 and scored on 3 of 5 power plays. Yaroslav Askarov allowed about three goals more than the shots he faced should have produced, while Darcy Kuemper stopped 30 of 32.

San Jose got power-play goals from Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg, the latter on a 2 percent chance, but never got closer than four goals. The facts we have don't give either team's record or streak, so what the night settles is narrower: the Kings answered the overtime loss in October with their most lopsided result of the season series, and the Sharks leave with a night in goal that they will want to forget.
